purpose: How a gold-plating bench turns a failed or ugly plated piece into a named defect with an evidenced root cause and a defensible disposition: capturing the piece before it is altered, naming the defect from a shared class library, reading the three evidence axes (where on the piece, when in the run, which tank) to separate bath-wide from part-local causes, walking the cause trees for peeling and blistering, burning, dull or hazy deposits, pitting, staining and uneven coverage back to prep, chemistry or process, proving the suspected cause on coupons instead of on the customer's piece, routing the confirmed cause to the lane that owns the fix, and deciding release, release-with-disclosure, strip-and-replate under documented approval and stripping-safety obligation classes, or return — then feeding every diagnosis back into prevention so the same defect is not diagnosed twice.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

commercial plating and stripping chemistry only, operated per the specific product's technical data sheet; every operating parameter named here is treated as a mechanism (what it does, what moves it, how it is verified by the TDS or by measurement), never as an invented universal setpoint

the shop keeps the minimum evidence base this KB reasons over: one logbook row per run, one retained part and one ride-along witness coupon per run, and dated photographs of anything that comes back; where those are missing the diagnosis degrades to a hypothesis that must be labeled as one
tank correction, prep rework and electrical or racking changes belong to the sibling bench lanes; this KB diagnoses, evidences and routes, it never doses a tank or re-cuts a rack itself

any chemistry touched during diagnosis or rework carries the same obligation classes as plating (segregation, storage, labeling, PPE, ventilation, training, emergency readiness) with the jurisdiction's workplace and hazmat rules verified; cyanide-class solutions and acids are never mixed, never stored together and never share a drain

defect names and test classes are shared language rather than shop invention: published class structures exist for adhesion, porosity, thickness and corrosion testing, while the acceptance threshold for a given product is agreed per job, not assumed universal
exclusions: karat-color families, matching to a customer reference or witness sample, lighting-consistent visual evaluation, gloss expectations set by pre-plate finish and hue-tolerance agreement — the sibling Color & Appearance Control KB owns the appearance verdict; this KB accepts a confirmed deviation from it and assigns cause

thickness specification per wear class, XRF and coupon measurement method classes and their limits, adhesion test classes (tape, bend, thermal), batch sampling discipline and the measurement records that back a claim — the sibling Thickness, Adhesion & Verification KB proves the deposit; this KB consumes its verdict and never invents a measurement of its own

guaranteed wear-life or durability figures: any durability statement to a customer is backed by measurement or stated as an estimate that names the method behind it, never a number invented to close a complaint

approving regulated label terms ('gold plated', 'gold flashed', 'vermeil', 'gold filled', 'rolled gold'), fineness claims or nickel-release compliance — these are compliance classes tied to the selling jurisdiction; this KB flags any disposition that disturbs a label-relevant property and refers it for verification of current rules, and never approves a claim

bath analysis, replenishment, purification and contamination treatment — the bath-chemistry lane owns the tank; this KB names the suspected chemistry cause with the evidence that points at it and hands it over

performing surface preparation (polish, degrease, electroclean, pickle, activation, strike) or designing racks, thieves, shields and current schedules — the prep and process-execution lanes own those corrections; this KB routes the cause to them with an evidence pack
formulating plating or stripping chemistry from raw chemicals and improvising a procedure at the bench — commercial products used per their TDS and formal training are assumed throughout
personalized legal, medical or financial advice; nickel-sensitization, skin-reaction and chemical-exposure questions route to the relevant regulation classes and to professional care

competency_questions.question: A ring has come back with the gold lifting at one edge — how do I decide whether prep, chemistry or process caused it instead of guessing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVIDENCE_TRIAD fixes the cause to where on the piece, when in the run and which tank, and ADHESION_FAILURE_TREE names which interface let go and the candidate causes that fit that evidence

competency_questions.question: What do I do in the first ten minutes with a defective piece so the evidence still exists when I start diagnosing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEFECT_TRIAGE_INTAKE gives the quarantine, do-not-alter and dated-photograph discipline plus the run identifiers that must be recovered before anything is cleaned or re-polished

competency_questions.question: Everyone in the shop calls it 'cloudy' — how do we name defects so the same word means the same thing twice and the diagnosis is comparable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEFECT_TAXONOMY supplies the named defect classes with their distinguishing appearance and a retained photo library that a name is assigned against

competency_questions.question: The load came out brown and rough on the edges and points but fine on the flats — what is that pattern telling me?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BURN_HIGH_CURRENT_TREE reads the high-current geometry pattern and lists the candidate causes (current density above what the metal content, temperature and agitation support, depletion, missing thieving or shielding, crowded contacts) with the evidence that separates them

competency_questions.question: The tank used to give a clean bright deposit and now everything comes out dull or hazy — is that the bath or the parts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WITNESS_REPLAY_METHOD separates bath-wide from part-local by comparing the ride-along witness with the part, and DULL_HAZY_DEPOSIT_TREE lists the bath-aging and contamination classes to refer for analysis

competency_questions.question: Small pits and dark spots are showing up, some right away and some after a few days — gas, dirt, pores or staining, and which test tells them apart?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PITTING_POROSITY_TREE distinguishes gas pits, particulate and substrate porosity and names the porosity screen class used on a steel-bearing stack, and STAIN_SPOT_TREE separates rinse, handling and storage staining by timing and pattern

competency_questions.question: The recesses came out pale and one spot is bare — is that throwing power, a contact or mask problem, or gas shielding?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COVERAGE_GAP_TREE separates thin-in-recess (current distribution) from truly bare (contact, mask, gas or non-wetting) and names what evidence on the piece decides it

competency_questions.question: When is it legitimate to say the customer's own piece caused the failure, and what evidence do I need before saying it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NO_BLAME_EVIDENCE_RULE states that substrate blame is never the default, and SUBSTRATE_ORIGIN_HYPOTHESIS gives the control-in-the-same-load test that must pass before the piece is named as the cause

competency_questions.question: What experiment confirms a suspected cause without spending the customer's piece or the whole tank on a guess?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISCRIMINATING_TEST_DESIGN specifies a one-variable test on coupons or scrap with the predicted outcome written before the run, and WITNESS_REPLAY_METHOD supplies the baseline it is compared against

competency_questions.question: This job failed — do I release it, release it with disclosure, strip and replate it, or hand it back?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISPOSITION_DECISION names the four outcomes and what each requires, STRIP_FEASIBILITY_ASSESSMENT says whether the piece can survive stripping at all, and CUSTOMER_DISCLOSURE_HONESTY fixes what may and may not be said about the result

competency_questions.question: What must be in place before a customer's piece goes anywhere near stripper, and what does the second plating run have to do differently?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REWORK_APPROVAL_GATE requires documented approval that names the risks, STRIPPING_SAFETY_AND_WASTE states the obligation classes and the segregation hard line with its waste route, and REPLATE_PREP_RESET requires the replate to start from a full prep chain with the routed cause already corrected

competency_questions.question: After the fix, how do I know the cause is actually gone rather than hiding until the next busy week?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEFECT_LOG_AND_TRENDING records each diagnosis with its evidence and disposition so recurrence is visible, and PREVENTION_FEEDBACK_LOOP requires a named prevention change and a scheduled recurrence check before the case is closed

competency_questions.question: Who actually fixes this — which bench lane owns the confirmed cause, and what do I hand them so they can act without re-diagnosing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAUSE_LANE_ROUTING assigns the confirmed cause to exactly one of prep, chemistry or process with the evidence pack the lane needs, and COLOR_DEVIATION_CAUSE_ROUTE shows how a hue deviation is split between the appearance verdict and the cause lanes

glossary.definition: Two adhesion-failure appearances that carry different evidence: a blister is a local dome where the deposit has lifted over a trapped defect or gas pocket while the surrounding film still holds, whereas a peel or flake is a sheet of deposit separating along an interface. Blisters point at a localized prep or entrapment failure, sheets point at a whole-surface interface failure.

The brown, matte, powdery or rough deposit that forms where the local current density exceeds what the bath's metal content, temperature and agitation can support; it appears first at edges, points, corners and wire tips because current crowds there, and it is a distribution symptom as much as a chemistry symptom.

Gold that deposits chemically rather than electrolytically when a less noble metal is put into a gold solution without current; the resulting loose smut has essentially no adhesion, which is why live entry and an intact strike are the standard defenses and why 'it went in dead' is a real diagnostic question.

The free-and-cheap cleanliness gate: a properly cleaned surface holds an unbroken sheet of rinse water, while oil or residue makes the film break into droplets. A defect traced to a skipped or failed water-break check is a prep-lane cause, not a bath cause.

Entering the work into the tank with current already applied so the surface never sits in solution unpolarized; loss of live entry is one of the classic evidenced causes of poor adhesion and displacement smut on strike-less work.

A scrap piece or wire offcut of the same stack plated in the same load as the job, used for destructive tests and as the diagnostic control: if the coupon is good and the part is bad the cause is part-local (geometry, racking, masking, substrate), and if both are bad the cause is bath- or process-wide.

The cheap in-house porosity test class for iron-bearing substrates, in which an indicator reveals iron exposed at pores as colored spots; it matters because a pore through gold over a steel core drives fast local corrosion. The reagent class is kept away from acids as a standing safety rule.

The bench owner a confirmed root cause is routed to — prep (cleaning, polishing, activation, strike), chemistry (bath composition, contamination, aging) or process (current, racking, agitation, handling, time) — plus the boundary lane of substrate origin, which requires its own evidence before it may be used.

Removing the failed deposit chemically or electrolytically and plating the piece again as a new job; it is not a cosmetic touch-up, it consumes base metal and time, it carries the same chemical-safety obligation classes as plating, and on customer goods it needs documented approval before it starts.

The scheduled look-back that closes a diagnosis: after a prevention change, a named number of subsequent runs or a named period is inspected specifically for the same defect class, so that a fix is confirmed by absence of recurrence rather than by the relief of one good batch.

nodes.definition: The first ten minutes with a defective piece decide whether a real diagnosis is possible at all, because almost every instinctive reaction destroys evidence: wiping, re-buffing, re-dipping or 'just cleaning it up' erases the blister edge, the drip line and the smut that would have named the cause. Intake means isolating the piece and the rest of its batch from shipping, photographing it dated at bench light and again under a loupe or USB microscope on both the defect and an unaffected zone of the same piece for contrast, and recovering the identifiers that let the run be reconstructed: job number, run date, rack or barrel position, the tank sequence the piece went through, the operator, and the retained part and ride-along witness coupon from that load. It also means taking a neutral history from the customer or the counter — how long it was worn, what it was cleaned with, how it was stored — without leading the answer. The output is a defect intake record created before anyone has an opinion, and it is the only artifact every later step in this KB can rely on.

included: quarantine of the piece and its batch
dated photographs of defect and control zone before any handling
recovery of job, run, rack and tank identifiers
neutral customer history
excluded: assigning a cause at intake
cleaning, polishing or re-dipping the piece
measuring thickness or adhesion, which the verification sibling owns

pros.claim: Photographing before handling keeps every cause tree open instead of collapsing to guesswork
pros.example: a 10x photo of the lifted edge showing white nickel underneath rather than bare brass immediately fixes the failure at the gold-to-nickel interface

pros.claim: Quarantining the rest of the batch stops a systemic defect from shipping while it is still being diagnosed
pros.example: holding the other eleven bangles from the same rack when the first one comes back blistered

cons.claim: Intake discipline costs bench time on complaints that turn out to be trivial
cons.example: quarantining a whole load over a drying spot that a rinse and a wipe would have cleared in a minute

cons.claim: A neutral history depends on a customer's memory and willingness, so a key fact can be missing or wrong
cons.example: a piece described as 'never touched' that was actually cleaned in a household dip

failure_modes: polishing or re-dipping the returned piece before it is photographed, which erases the only evidence of the interface that failed
accepting a piece back with no job or run identifier so no run can be replayed and every later conclusion is speculation
letting the piece sit loose on the bench where it gets confused with current production
acceptance_tests: the intake record carries dated photographs of the defect and of a good zone on the same piece, the job and run identifiers, the rack or barrel position where known, and the customer history statement
the rest of the affected batch is physically quarantined and marked before any diagnosis begins
revisit_triggers: a returned piece arrives already cleaned, polished or re-plated elsewhere
the identifiers on the intake record match no logged run

base.update_signal: a diagnosis stalls because a piece was altered or unidentified at intake

nodes.definition: The standing attribution rule of this subdomain: the customer's piece is never the default suspect, and neither is the newest employee. A shop that reaches for 'porous casting' or 'that piece was junk' as its first explanation ends the investigation exactly where its own repeatable cause lives, and it does so in the one direction that also costs it the customer. The rule states that any substrate-origin attribution must clear three bars — a known-good control plated in the same load that came out clean, a defect pattern that follows the piece rather than its rack position or the tank state, and something visible or testable on the piece itself such as a gas-porous casting face, a lead-bearing solder seam or an unidentified prior coating. Until those bars are cleared the working assumption is that something the shop controls (prep, chemistry or process) produced the defect. The same rule governs language: a hypothesis is spoken as a hypothesis to the customer, never as a verdict about their goods.

included: default attribution to shop-controlled causes until evidence moves it
the three bars a substrate claim must clear
how a hypothesis is spoken before it is confirmed
excluded: the substrate test procedure itself
commercial negotiation over who pays
intake documentation of pre-existing damage, which belongs to the job-intake lane

pros.claim: Refusing the easy blame keeps the shop's own repeatable causes visible instead of hidden behind a story
pros.example: the third 'bad casting' complaint in a month turning out to be one rack whose contact fingers had lost tension

pros.claim: Hypothesis-shaped language protects the relationship while the diagnosis is still open
pros.example: telling a customer the seam area is being tested as a possible source rather than announcing their piece was contaminated

cons.claim: Holding the shop as first suspect can absorb cost and time on jobs where the incoming goods really were unplateable
cons.example: twice re-prepping a pot-metal costume piece before the control coupon finally shows the substrate is the limit

cons.claim: The rule can be misread as never telling a customer an uncomfortable truth about their goods
cons.example: delaying an honest conversation about a lead-soldered antique until after a failed rework

failure_modes: declaring a substrate cause with no control piece in the same load to compare against
using the rule as a reason never to state an evidenced substrate limitation, so bad work is repeated at the shop's expense
acceptance_tests: every closed diagnosis that names a substrate cause cites a same-load control result and a piece-specific observation
no customer-facing message asserts a substrate cause while the diagnosis is still labeled unconfirmed
revisit_triggers: substrate causes start rising as a share of the defect log without matching control evidence
a lane pushes back that it is being blamed without evidence

base.update_signal: a closed case is reopened because a substrate attribution failed to hold up

nodes.definition: A defect that is not named the same way twice cannot be diagnosed, trended or handed to another lane, so this unit fixes the shop's vocabulary: peel or flake (sheet separation at an interface), blister (local dome with the film still attached around it), burn (brown matte roughness at high-current geometry), dull or hazy deposit (whole-surface loss of brightness at normal thickness), pit (discrete depression in the deposit), pore-driven spot (corrosion product appearing at a point days later), stain or water spot (surface film following drip or contact patterns), skip or bare area (no deposit at all), thin-in-recess (deposit present but visibly weak in shielded geometry), contact mark (rack or barrel witness point), and smut or displacement deposit (loose dark powder with no adhesion). Each class carries its distinguishing appearance and the single question that separates it from its nearest neighbour, and each is anchored to photographs of the shop's own past examples rather than to a memory of what somebody once called cloudy.

included: named defect classes with distinguishing appearance
the separating question between neighbouring classes
the retained defect photo library and how entries are added
excluded: cause assignment, which the cause trees own
color tolerance judgment against a master panel, which the appearance sibling owns
pass or fail thresholds for measured properties

pros.claim: A named class makes trending possible, so recurrence becomes visible instead of anecdotal
pros.example: counting eleven blister cases against two burn cases in a quarter and seeing immediately which lane to work on

pros.claim: A photo library settles arguments about what the piece actually shows in seconds
pros.example: holding the returned pendant next to the library image of a contact mark and closing the 'is it a pit' debate

cons.claim: Real pieces often show two classes at once, so a single-name habit hides the second defect
cons.example: a hazy bangle that is also blistered at the bail, where only the haze gets recorded

cons.claim: Maintaining the library takes discipline nobody is paid for and it decays quietly
cons.example: a library whose last entry is two years old while the shop has since changed underplate

failure_modes: inventing a new informal word for a defect the library already names, which breaks trending
recording only the most visible defect on a piece that shows several
acceptance_tests: every logged defect carries a class name drawn from the library plus at least one photograph attached to that entry
a piece showing more than one class is recorded with all of them, in the order the evidence supports
revisit_triggers: a defect appears that no existing class describes
a change of underplate, bath or supplier product changes what a class looks like

base.update_signal: a defect arrives that the class list cannot name, or a process change alters a class appearance

nodes.definition: The diagnostic engine of this subdomain is three questions asked before any hypothesis is allowed. WHERE on the piece: high-current edges, points and wire tips, or shielded recesses and insides of rings, or exactly at contact and hanging points, or the whole surface uniformly, or one face only. WHEN in the run and in the calendar: the first pieces or the last, the whole load or only the tail, this run alone or a slow drift across weeks, visible at unracking or only after drying, or only after days in the customer's hands. WHICH tank or step the pattern points at: soak clean, electroclean, pickle, activation, strike, underplate, gold, rinse or dry. Each axis eliminates whole families of cause — a defect at high-current geometry cannot be a soak-clean failure, a defect that arrived gradually over weeks is not a one-off racking error, and a defect on every piece including the witness coupon cannot be about that customer's piece. The triad is recorded as answered or explicitly unknown, because an unrecorded axis is the usual reason two people reach two different confident conclusions.

included: the location, timing and tank axes and what each eliminates
recording unknown answers as unknown
the combination rule that narrows to a cause family
excluded: the detailed cause list per defect class, which each tree owns
instrumented measurement of the deposit
correcting whatever the triad points at

pros.claim: Three cheap questions eliminate most candidate causes before anyone touches a tank
pros.example: burn only on the ring's outer edge with the recess perfect, which rules out the whole 'bath is exhausted' story and points at current distribution

pros.claim: Explicitly recording an unknown axis stops false confidence from filling the gap
pros.example: an unrecorded rack position leaving 'bad bath' and 'bad contact' equally open, and the log saying so

cons.claim: The timing axis depends on records that a busy shop may not have kept
cons.example: no logbook row for the night run, so 'first or last piece' can no longer be answered

cons.claim: Patterns can overlap and point at two families at once, which the triad alone cannot split
cons.example: a defect at both the contact point and the high-current edge, where racking and current density both remain live

failure_modes: jumping to the shop's favourite cause before the three axes are answered
treating a missing record as evidence of absence rather than as an unknown
answering the axes from memory days later instead of from the intake record and logbook
acceptance_tests: the diagnosis sheet shows an explicit answer or an explicit unknown for each of location, timing and tank before any candidate cause is written down
at least one candidate cause is struck out by an axis answer rather than by preference
revisit_triggers: new evidence arrives that changes an axis answer, such as a second returned piece from a different rack position
the routed lane reports that the pattern does not match what their equipment could produce

base.update_signal: a confirmed cause turns out to contradict the recorded axis answers

nodes.definition: Before theorizing, reconstruct the run from what it left behind: the ride-along witness coupon of the same stack plated in the same load, the retained part kept from that batch, the logbook row naming bath, load, time, rack layout and operator, and the retained parts of the runs immediately before and after from the same tank. The comparison is a decision table. Coupon clean and part defective means the cause is part-local — geometry, rack position, masking, handling or the substrate. Coupon and part both defective means the cause is bath-wide or process-wide and no amount of re-prepping that one piece will fix it. Earlier runs from the same tank clean, this one not, means something changed between them: a new load type, a drag-in event, a fresh addition, a different operator or a longer idle. Progressive degradation across many runs means aging, contamination build-up or accumulating drag-in rather than a single mistake. This unit is what makes the difference between a diagnosis and an opinion, and its cost is the discipline of keeping the coupons and the log in the first place.

included: coupon versus part comparison
reading the logbook row and neighbouring runs
the bath-wide versus part-local decision table
excluded: analysing the bath, which the chemistry lane performs
measuring the coupon to a thickness class, which the verification sibling owns
designing the new experiment, which the discriminating-test unit owns

pros.claim: One coupon comparison answers the most expensive question in the shop for free
pros.example: a clean witness beside a blistered ring immediately saving a tank from being needlessly dumped or dosed

pros.claim: Neighbouring runs date the onset, which turns a vague complaint into a bounded window to investigate
pros.example: clean retained parts through Tuesday and haze from Wednesday onward, bracketing the change to one day

cons.claim: The method collapses when the shop skipped coupons or logging on the run in question
cons.example: a rush job run without a witness where the only piece available is the customer's

cons.claim: A flat coupon does not experience the same current distribution as a complex piece, so it can pass while a real geometry fails legitimately
cons.example: a flat witness looking perfect while the deep recess of a signet ring is starved

failure_modes: treating a passing witness coupon as proof the whole load is fine, when the coupon geometry cannot show recess starvation
consuming the retained part in a destructive test before the comparison is made
comparing against a retained part from a different bath state and drawing a false conclusion
acceptance_tests: the diagnosis sheet records the coupon result, the retained-part result and the logbook row for the run before a cause family is chosen
the bath-wide versus part-local call is stated explicitly with the comparison that supports it
revisit_triggers: coupons or retained parts are found missing for the affected run
a later measurement contradicts the bath-wide or part-local call

base.update_signal: a run is diagnosed without a coupon or retained part, or a coupon result is contradicted by the piece

nodes.definition: When the evidence narrows to two or three candidate causes, the way out is a deliberately designed experiment rather than a change made hopefully in production. The design rules are short and strict: write the prediction before the run so the result can disagree with you, change exactly one variable, run it on coupons or scrap of the same stack rather than on customer goods, and inspect it the same way the defect was first inspected. Typical bench experiments are a re-clean and re-plate of a scrap piece with the cleaning step deliberately extended to test a prep hypothesis, a graded-current panel to find where burn begins on this bath and this geometry, a coupon plated with and without the strike to test an adhesion hypothesis, a re-run of the same rack position with a fresh contact to test a racking hypothesis, and a soak of a defective piece to test whether a stain is a surface film or a corrosion product. The stop rule matters as much as the design: after two ambiguous tests the case is routed to a lane as an unconfirmed most-likely cause rather than dressed up as a fact.

included: one-variable coupon experiments with a written prediction
the standard bench experiment set for this subdomain
the two-ambiguous-results stop rule
excluded: bath analysis and additions, which the chemistry lane runs
accredited or instrumented testing for claims, which is a send-out class
experiments performed on the customer's piece

pros.claim: A written prediction converts a habit into evidence, because the shop can be shown wrong on paper
pros.example: predicting that the extended clean will stop the blistering and finding it unchanged, which redirects the search to the strike

pros.claim: Coupons make the experiment cheap enough to actually run instead of being skipped under deadline
pros.example: three wire offcuts and ten minutes settling a debate that had been running for two weeks

cons.claim: One-variable discipline is slow when several plausible causes are stacked, and deadlines push toward changing everything at once
cons.example: a shop that re-cleans, re-racks and adjusts current together and learns nothing from the good result

cons.claim: Coupon geometry and mass differ from the real piece, so a negative coupon result does not always exonerate a cause
cons.example: a flat coupon that never reproduces the gas entrapment happening inside a hollow bead

failure_modes: changing more than one variable and losing the ability to attribute the improvement
running the test on the customer's piece because it is the only example available
declaring a cause confirmed after an ambiguous result because the schedule needs an answer
acceptance_tests: each test record carries the written prediction, the single variable changed, the substrate and stack used, and the observed result
no confirmed-cause entry in the defect log rests on a test run on customer goods or on a multi-variable change
revisit_triggers: two consecutive tests return ambiguous results
the routed lane's correction fails to remove the defect, invalidating the confirmed cause

base.update_signal: a confirmed cause fails to reproduce or a lane correction does not remove the defect

nodes.definition: Peeling, flaking and blistering are diagnosed by first answering which interface let go, because the answer selects the cause family. Lift the loose film at the edge under magnification and look at what is exposed: bright white metal means the gold released from the nickel underplate, yellow or red base metal means the nickel released from the substrate, and a dull grey powder that wipes away means a displacement deposit that never adhered at all. Gold-from-nickel failures point at the nickel having passivated between steps — a delay, a dry-out, an interrupted transfer, a missing or exhausted gold strike, or entry into the gold tank without current so the surface displacement-plated instead of electroplating. Nickel-from-substrate failures point back at cleaning and activation: an oil film that a water-break check would have caught, incomplete oxide removal, or a passive surface such as stainless entering without the strike class its specification calls for. Blisters localized to one zone rather than the whole surface usually mean entrapment — porosity, a seam, a crevice or trapped process solution — while sheets over the whole piece mean the interface was wrong everywhere. Thickness and stack brittleness are the remaining branch: an over-thick or brightener-embrittled underplate cracks and lifts on forming or on impact even when the interface was sound.

included: interface identification from what lies under the lifted film
passivation, strike, live-entry and cleanliness branches
entrapment versus whole-surface reasoning
stack brittleness as a distinct branch
excluded: running the adhesion test classes themselves, which the verification sibling owns
re-designing the prep chain or the strike, which the prep lane owns
the decision to strip and replate

pros.claim: Naming the failed interface cuts the candidate list roughly in half before any test is run
pros.example: white nickel visible under a lifted flake immediately clearing the degrease step and pointing at the gold strike and transfer discipline

pros.claim: The localized-versus-whole-surface split separates a piece problem from a process problem without instruments
pros.example: blisters only along a soldered seam on one piece while the rest of the load is sound

cons.claim: Adhesion failures often have two contributing causes and fixing only the obvious one lets it recur
cons.example: restoring live entry while the real driver, a long wet-transfer delay at shift change, stays untouched

cons.claim: Interface reading needs magnification and a steady hand, and a badly lifted film can be ambiguous
cons.example: a flake that curled and folded in the customer's pocket so both faces look alike at 10x

failure_modes: calling every peel a cleaning problem because that is the most familiar cause
re-plating over a lifting deposit instead of stripping, which reproduces the failure on the new layer
ignoring the transfer and delay evidence because it lives in operator habit rather than in a tank reading
acceptance_tests: the diagnosis names the failed interface with the observation that identified it and lists the branch causes consistent with the run evidence
any adhesion conclusion is cross-checked against the ride-along witness before a lane is assigned
revisit_triggers: the same interface fails again after the routed correction
a change of underplate chemistry, strike product or transfer sequence enters the shop

base.update_signal: an adhesion diagnosis is contradicted by the replate outcome or by a lane's correction result

nodes.definition: A brown, matte, rough or powdery deposit concentrated at edges, points, corners, prongs and wire tips is the signature of local current density running beyond what the bath can feed at that spot, and the tree walks the four things that set that balance. First is the current itself relative to the actual loaded area, which is where an estimated rather than a computed area quietly doubles the density on a light load. Second is what the bath can supply: metal content, temperature and agitation set the limit, they interact, and their working window is a property of the specific commercial product read from its technical data sheet and the shop's own logged runs rather than a number to be assumed. Third is distribution hardware — missing or misplaced thieves and shields, work hung too close to an anode, crowded rack spacing — which concentrates current on geometry that was never meant to carry it. Fourth is contact and connection quality, where a poor or arcing contact heats and burns locally while the rest of the piece looks fine. The triad evidence separates them: burn on every piece at the same geometry is a current or bath-supply story, burn only on the outermost positions is a distribution story, and burn only at the hanger is a contact story.

included: current-versus-loaded-area reasoning
bath supply limits as TDS-governed mechanisms
thieving, shielding and spacing as distribution causes
contact and arcing as a local cause
excluded: setting the current schedule or redesigning racks, which the process-execution lane owns
analysing or replenishing the bath, which the chemistry lane owns
declaring a numeric current density limit as universal fact

pros.claim: Reading burn as a distribution symptom stops the shop from dosing a healthy tank
pros.example: burnt prongs on the two outer positions only, with the middle of the rack perfect and the witness clean

pros.claim: The loaded-area question catches the most common quiet error in small-shop plating
pros.example: a half-empty rack run at the same setting as a full one and burning every edge in the load

cons.claim: Burn and depletion can look alike at the piece, and separating them needs the log or an analysis the diagnosis lane cannot perform
cons.example: an end-of-day run burning because metal content fell rather than because current rose

cons.claim: Chasing burn by lowering current can starve recesses and trade one defect for another
cons.example: clean edges after a current reduction, with pale under-covered recesses appearing on the next batch

failure_modes: adjusting current from feel without recording the loaded area that made the old setting wrong
blaming the bath for a hanging geometry that concentrates current on one edge every single run
quoting a current density figure as universal instead of reading the product's data sheet and the shop's logged runs
acceptance_tests: the diagnosis states the loaded area used, the rack positions affected and whether the witness burned, before a cause is named
any bath-supply hypothesis is handed to the chemistry lane for analysis rather than acted on at the tank by this lane
revisit_triggers: burn recurs after the distribution or current correction
a new part geometry, rack design or load size enters production

base.update_signal: a burn case is resolved by a cause outside this tree, or the product data sheet revises its operating window

nodes.definition: When brightness falls away across a whole load and the pre-plate finish was as good as it always is, the cause is usually in the tank or in the layer beneath rather than in the gold itself, and the tree separates four families. Bath aging is first: alkaline cyanide baths accumulate carbonate over time and organics accumulate from drag-in, breakdown and airborne shop dust, and both flatten a deposit; published handbook ranges exist for tolerable levels, but the number that matters is the one in the product's technical data sheet against an actual analysis, which is the chemistry lane's work rather than a bench guess. Metallic contamination is second and usually arrives with a color change as well as a haze. The layer beneath is third — a dull, etched or unlevelled underplate shows straight through thin gold, so a nickel bath losing its leveller or a change of pre-plate finish presents at the gold as haze. Rinse and dry residue is fourth and is distinguished by being removable: a film that wipes or re-rinses away was never a deposit property. The discriminator is the witness coupon plus the trend of retained parts, which separates a step change from a slow decline.

included: bath aging and contamination families as referral hypotheses
underplate and pre-plate finish showing through thin gold
removable film versus deposit property test
step change versus slow decline reading
excluded: carbonate removal, carbon treatment or any bath correction, which the chemistry lane performs
judging brightness against a customer reference, which the appearance sibling owns
asserting a numeric contamination threshold

pros.claim: The wipe test separates a residue from a real deposit property in seconds and saves a tank from unnecessary treatment
pros.example: a milky film on a batch of earrings that disappears with a re-rinse, ending the investigation at the rinse tank

pros.claim: Looking beneath the gold catches the common case where the underplate, not the gold bath, lost its brightness
pros.example: haze appearing on every job in the week after the nickel bath's leveller ran down

cons.claim: Bath-aging hypotheses cannot be confirmed at the bench, so the diagnosis stalls until an analysis is available
cons.example: a suspected carbonate build-up waiting on the analysis the chemistry lane has to schedule

cons.claim: Slow decline is easy to normalize, so the shop's eye adapts and the reference drifts with it
cons.example: months of gradually flatter deposits accepted as normal until a customer holds an old piece against a new one

failure_modes: treating the gold bath as the suspect while a dull underplate is doing all the work
acting on a guessed contamination level instead of referring it for analysis against the product data sheet
recording haze without keeping the retained part that would have shown when the decline started
acceptance_tests: the diagnosis records whether the witness coupon is also dull, whether the film is removable, and whether retained parts show a step change or a decline
any bath-aging or contamination hypothesis is handed over as a referral with its evidence rather than acted on at the tank
revisit_triggers: the chemistry lane's analysis contradicts the referred hypothesis
a change of underplate product, pre-plate finish or shop ventilation coincides with the haze

base.update_signal: an analysis result or an underplate change explains a haze case this tree attributed elsewhere

nodes.definition: Pits and pores look similar on day one and behave very differently by week three, so the tree splits them by origin and by timing. Gas pitting comes from hydrogen bubbles clinging to the surface during deposition and leaves round, often upward-facing pits or teardrop trails; it points at agitation, wetting and part orientation rather than at chemistry. Particulate pitting comes from solids in the bath or from airborne dust landing on a wet surface and leaves irregular pits, often with a nucleus, and it points at filtration and housekeeping. Substrate porosity comes from the piece itself — a gas-porous casting face, an open seam, a sintered or worn area — and it reproduces in the same places on the same piece no matter how many times it is re-run. True coating porosity is different again: pores are through-paths that only announce themselves later as corrosion spots, and on a steel-bearing stack they matter disproportionately because gold is cathodic to steel, so a pore becomes a driven corrosion cell rather than a cosmetic point. The screening method class for iron-bearing substrates is an indicator test read after the deposit has aged rather than straight out of the dryer, since fresh rinse residue plugs pores and produces a falsely clean result.

included: gas, particulate, substrate and coating-porosity branches
timing as the discriminator between a pit and a pore
the pore-plus-steel corrosion mechanism
the aged-deposit rule for porosity screening
excluded: formal porosity or corrosion test classes used to support a claim, which are the verification sibling's and send-out classes
filtration and agitation equipment changes, which the process lane owns
quoting a pore-count acceptance number as universal

pros.claim: Splitting pits by shape and orientation points at agitation and filtration without any instrument
pros.example: round pits only on upward-facing surfaces of every piece in the load, which reads as clinging gas rather than dirt

pros.claim: Understanding that a pore over a steel core drives corrosion prevents a cosmetic disposition of a structural problem
pros.example: treating a single dark spot on a plated steel cuff as a pore through the stack rather than as a smudge

cons.claim: Porosity evidence usually arrives late, after the piece has been sold and worn, when the run evidence has gone cold
cons.example: rust points reported three weeks after delivery on a run whose coupon is long since discarded

cons.claim: Substrate porosity and coating porosity can coexist, and separating them takes a re-plate of the same piece nobody wants to fund
cons.example: a cast pendant that pits in the same two places after every attempt

failure_modes: screening for porosity immediately after plating and recording a false clean result
calling every late-appearing dark spot a stain when it is corrosion product coming through a pore
assuming a thicker deposit alone will close pores without addressing the underplate or the substrate surface
acceptance_tests: the diagnosis records pit shape, orientation and distribution and whether the spots appeared at unracking or in service
any porosity screening result cited is taken on an aged deposit and on worst-case zones rather than on proud flats only
revisit_triggers: field returns show corrosion points on a run previously screened clean
the substrate class, underplate thickness or filtration setup changes

base.update_signal: a field return or an aged screening result contradicts the pit-versus-pore call made at the bench

nodes.definition: Staining is diagnosed by pattern and by timing, because the marks themselves are generic. Drip lines, tide marks and spots that follow gravity or the hanging orientation point at rinsing and drying: incompletely rinsed process chemistry left to dry on the surface, hard water drying in place, or a piece dried in still air with solution trapped in a crevice or a hollow. Marks that follow contact point at handling — bare fingers on a warm deposit, a dirty bench mat, tissue fibres, or a rack pad that transferred residue. Marks that arrive days later and grow point at something chemically active: corrosion product coming up through a pore, sulfur-bearing packaging, rubber bands or foam in contact with the piece, or a base metal exposed at a wear point. The single most useful bench discriminator is whether the mark can be removed: a film that lifts with a clean re-rinse or a gentle approved cleaning was a residue and the case ends at the rinse or handling step, while a mark that returns or that sits under the deposit is a coating or substrate matter that belongs in the porosity or adhesion trees. Storage and packaging are part of the tree, not an afterthought, because plenty of perfect work is spoiled after it leaves the tank.

included: rinse, dry, handling, storage and packaging branches
removable-versus-returning as the bench discriminator
pattern reading by gravity, contact and timing
excluded: corrosion testing classes used for claims
rinse-water treatment engineering and dryer selection, which the process lane owns
prescribing a consumer cleaning product to a customer

pros.claim: Pattern reading resolves most staining cases at zero cost and keeps them out of the rework queue
pros.example: identical tide marks at the same height on every piece hung the same way, which names the drying step immediately

pros.claim: Including packaging and storage in the tree catches defects created after a perfect run
pros.example: darkening only where the pendant rested against a rubber band in the display box

cons.claim: Removing a stain to test it can also remove the evidence needed if the case turns out to be corrosion
cons.example: cleaning a spot away before photographing it, then being unable to show whether it was returning

cons.claim: Customer-side handling is hard to establish and the answer often stays probabilistic
cons.example: a pattern consistent with a household cleaning dip that the customer does not recall using

failure_modes: cleaning the piece before the mark is photographed and characterized
recording a late-appearing corrosion spot as a handling stain and closing the case
treating every stain as a customer problem without checking whether the whole load shows the same pattern
acceptance_tests: the diagnosis records the mark's pattern, its timing and whether it is removable, with a photograph taken before any cleaning
a mark that returns after removal is escalated into the porosity or adhesion tree rather than closed as a stain
revisit_triggers: the same stain pattern appears across different jobs and operators
a change of rinse water, dryer, packaging material or storage location

base.update_signal: a stain classed as removable residue returns in service or proves to be corrosion product

nodes.definition: Uneven coverage splits into two very different problems that look alike at arm's length: deposit present but weak, and deposit absent. Thin-in-recess is a current-distribution matter — shielded geometry inside rings, under bezels, between links and behind stones receives less current than the outside, and how much less depends on the bath's throwing power, the anode arrangement, the rack geometry and the agitation. Truly bare areas have discrete causes instead: a contact or hanging point that was shadowed by its own fixture, a masked or taped area whose edge bled, a gas pocket that sat in a hollow or a blind recess and kept solution off the surface, a non-wetting residue that survived cleaning, tangled or nested work in a barrel, or a contact that lost connection mid-run. The evidence separates them cleanly: a gradient that fades smoothly into the recess is distribution, while a hard-edged area with a sharp boundary is a mask, a contact or a bubble. Barrel work adds its own signature, with nesting and shadowing producing patchy, position-dependent coverage across the load rather than a repeatable pattern on each piece. This tree diagnoses and evidences; the fixture, mask and current corrections belong to the process-execution lane.

included: thin-in-recess versus bare-area separation
contact, mask, gas and non-wetting branches
barrel nesting and shadowing signatures
gradient versus hard edge as the evidence rule
excluded: designing racks, thieves, shields or masks, which the process lane owns
measuring recess thickness to a class, which the verification sibling owns
changing the bath to improve throwing power

pros.claim: The gradient-versus-hard-edge rule sorts most coverage complaints in one look
pros.example: a sharp crescent of bare brass at the bail exactly where the hook sat, which is a fixture story not a bath story

pros.claim: Separating thin from bare stops the shop from raising current on what is actually a masking or contact fault
pros.example: a bare spot inside a ring shank blamed on throwing power until the rack hook mark is matched to it

cons.claim: Recess thinness is invisible to the eye at some thickness classes, so appearance under-reports the problem
cons.example: a recess that looks covered but measures far below the outside face when the verification lane checks it

cons.claim: Fixing recess coverage often means re-fixturing or re-running, which costs more than the job earned
cons.example: a linked bracelet that needs individual hanging rather than a single hook to cover the link interiors

failure_modes: raising current to chase recess coverage and burning the outer geometry instead
reporting coverage as acceptable from appearance alone when the significant surface was never measured by the verification lane
moving a contact point without recording where the old one was, so the next batch shows a new mark nobody can explain
acceptance_tests: the diagnosis states whether the affected zone is thin or bare, with the gradient or hard-edge evidence that decided it, and marks the fixture contact positions used on the run
any recess-thickness question is referred to the verification lane rather than settled by eye
revisit_triggers: a new part geometry, fixture or masking method enters production
the verification lane reports recess thickness failures on parts this tree passed as covered

base.update_signal: a measured recess result or a fixture change contradicts the thin-versus-bare call

nodes.definition: Color is judged elsewhere and diagnosed here. Once the appearance lane has confirmed against its master panel and defined light that a deposit really is off-target — not a lighting artifact, not an untrained eye — this unit assigns the deviation a cause family. A red, brassy or grey cast that arrives across a whole load usually points at metallic contamination dragged into the bath or dissolved from attacked fixtures, and it belongs to the chemistry lane as an analysis referral. A gradual hue drift over weeks in an alloyed or hardened system points at the alloying constituent or the operating window moving, which is again a chemistry and process referral rather than a bench adjustment. A tone that changes with position on the piece, or that differs between the flats and the recesses, points at current density and distribution and belongs with the coverage and burn trees. A tone that looks thin or shows the layer beneath points at thickness and at the underplate rather than at the gold bath, and it goes to the verification lane to confirm the deposit before anyone touches chemistry. The boundary rule is strict in both directions: this unit never re-judges whether the color is acceptable, and it never lets a hue complaint become a claim about karat, fineness or a regulated label term.

included: cause families for a confirmed color deviation
routing hue evidence to chemistry, process or verification
the boundary against re-judging appearance and against label claims
excluded: judging color against a reference or master panel, which the appearance sibling owns
lighting method and tolerance agreement
any statement about karat, fineness or a regulated label term

pros.claim: Treating a confirmed hue shift as evidence rather than as taste gives the chemistry lane an early, cheap warning
pros.example: a grey cast across a whole load arriving days before adhesion trouble, and being referred for analysis on the strength of the color alone

pros.claim: The position-dependent versus load-wide split stops color complaints being pushed at the bath by default
pros.example: a warmer tone only inside the ring shank, which is a distribution question rather than a contamination question

cons.claim: Color causes overlap heavily and the bench can rarely close one without an analysis it does not perform
cons.example: a brassy tone that could be drag-in contamination or simply thin gold over a warm underplate

cons.claim: The hand-off boundary adds a step and can feel bureaucratic when the same person wears both hats in a small shop
cons.example: one operator having to record the appearance verdict before writing the cause referral for the same piece

failure_modes: diagnosing a color cause from a deviation that was never confirmed under the appearance lane's method
letting a color conversation drift into a karat or label claim
referring every hue complaint to the bath when thickness or underplate explains it
acceptance_tests: every color cause referral cites the appearance lane's confirmed deviation and names one cause family with its evidence
no color diagnosis in the log contains a fineness, karat or regulated label statement
revisit_triggers: an analysis or thickness result contradicts the referred color cause
a new bath product, alloy system or underplate changes the shop's baseline tone

base.update_signal: a referred color cause is disproved by analysis, thickness measurement or a product change

nodes.definition: Sometimes the piece genuinely cannot be plated well as received, and this unit is how that is proven rather than asserted. The recognizable classes are a gas-porous or shrinkage-porous casting face that outgasses and blisters wherever it is thin, a soldered seam whose filler behaves differently in cleaning and plating than the parent metal, an unidentified prior coating or lacquer that no standard activation removes, zinc-bearing pot metal and low-melting alloys that the prep chain attacks, a piece worn so thin at a shank or a wear point that the base is no longer continuous, and set stones, pearls, resins or organics that limit which prep and which chemistry may be used at all. The proof standard is fixed: a known-good control of the shop's normal work plated in the same load must come out clean, the defect must follow the piece across a re-run rather than following the position or the tank state, and there must be an observation on the piece itself that names the class. When the standard is met, the finding is documented with photographs and communicated as a limitation of the goods with options, not as a verdict on the customer; when it is not met, the case returns to the shop-controlled lanes.

included: the recognizable substrate limitation classes
the three-part proof standard including a same-load control
documenting and communicating a proven limitation with options
excluded: intake assessment and quoting of incoming goods, which the job-intake lane owns
metallurgical identification beyond what the bench can evidence
refusing work on suspicion without a control result

pros.claim: A same-load control turns an accusation into a demonstration a customer can see
pros.example: the shop's own test ring coming out flawless beside the customer's cast pendant that blistered in the same basket

pros.claim: Naming the substrate class early prevents a rework cycle that would have failed identically
pros.example: recognizing lacquer on an inherited piece before stripping and replating it twice

cons.claim: The proof standard costs a run and a control piece, which is real money on a small job
cons.example: plating a control alongside a single repair earring to settle a dispute worth less than the run

cons.claim: Substrate classes overlap with prep failures and the bench cannot always tell them apart without destructive work
cons.example: porosity in a seam that could equally be trapped flux from an earlier repair

failure_modes: declaring a substrate cause without a control in the same load, which is the blame default in disguise
treating a suspected substrate limit as proven and skipping the prep hypotheses that would have fixed it
communicating the finding as a judgment about the customer's goods rather than as a documented limitation with options
acceptance_tests: every substrate attribution in the log cites a same-load control result, a follow-the-piece observation and a named class
the customer-facing message for a substrate finding states the evidence and the options rather than assigning fault
revisit_triggers: a control result comes back defective, invalidating the substrate attribution
a piece attributed to substrate origin later plates cleanly after a prep change

base.update_signal: a substrate attribution is overturned by a later clean plate of the same piece

nodes.definition: A diagnosis that stays inside the quality bench changes nothing, so the confirmed cause is routed to the one lane that can act on it: prep (cleaning, polishing, degrease, electroclean, pickle, activation, strike discipline and transfer timing), chemistry (bath composition, contamination, aging, additions and analysis), process (current and loaded area, racking and contacts, thieving and shielding, agitation, time, handling and drying), or the boundary lane of substrate origin, which may only be used when its own proof standard is met. Routing is single-owner on purpose: a cause sent to everybody is owned by nobody and comes back unfixed. The handover is an evidence pack, not a complaint — the defect class and photographs, the three axis answers, the witness and retained-part comparison, the discriminating test with its written prediction and result, and the one change being asked for. Where the evidence supports two lanes, the pack names a primary and a secondary with the observation that would decide between them, and the case stays open in the log until the primary lane reports back.

included: the four lane definitions and the single-owner rule
the contents of an evidence pack
primary and secondary routing with a deciding observation
excluded: performing the correction in any lane
approving a bath addition or a rack redesign
assigning commercial responsibility or cost between shop and customer

pros.claim: Single-owner routing makes a fix traceable to a person and a change instead of to a general resolution
pros.example: handing the strike and transfer-timing case to the prep lane with a photograph of the nickel-side interface and one requested change

pros.claim: An evidence pack stops the receiving lane from re-diagnosing from scratch and disagreeing on the facts
pros.example: the chemistry lane opening a haze referral that already contains the coupon result and the retained-part trend

cons.claim: In a one-person shop the lanes are the same human, so the discipline can feel like paperwork and quietly lapse
cons.example: the plater who diagnosed the burn simply turning the current down without ever writing the routing entry

cons.claim: Forcing a single owner can mis-assign genuinely shared causes and delay the fix
cons.example: a defect that needs both a longer clean and a re-hung rack being sent only to prep

failure_modes: routing a cause that is still unconfirmed as though it were established fact
sending the same case to several lanes so each waits for the others
closing the routing entry before the receiving lane reports what it changed and what happened
acceptance_tests: every routed case names one primary lane, the single change requested, and the evidence pack contents attached to it
cases remain open in the defect log until the receiving lane records the change made and its outcome
revisit_triggers: the receiving lane reports the requested change did not alter the defect
a lane's share of routed causes shifts sharply, suggesting the routing rule is mis-set

base.update_signal: a routed correction fails to remove the defect, or lane ownership of a cause class changes

nodes.definition: Diagnosis and disposition are separate decisions and this unit makes the second one explicitly, with four outcomes and a stated requirement for each. Release applies when the defect is cosmetic within the tolerance agreed for the job and the verification lane's thickness and adhesion verdict is in hand; appearance alone never releases a piece whose deposit was never proven. Release with disclosure applies when the piece is serviceable but visibly imperfect or built to a lighter class than intended, and it requires the customer to be told what they are receiving in plain language before delivery, without any invented durability figure. Rework by strip and replate applies when the defect is structural — adhesion failure, bare areas on wear surfaces, pores through to a corroding base — and the piece can survive stripping and the customer has approved it. Return applies when rework risk is unacceptable, when the substrate limitation is proven, or when the shop cannot produce the specified result on that piece. Any disposition that would change a label-relevant property, such as dropping below a thickness class or removing base metal from a silver piece, is flagged for compliance verification in the selling jurisdiction rather than decided at the bench.

included: the four dispositions and what each requires
the rule that release needs the verification verdict, not just a nice appearance
flagging label-relevant consequences for compliance verification
excluded: performing the measurement that supports release, which the verification sibling owns
approving a regulated label term or a compliance claim
pricing, refund and warranty negotiation

pros.claim: Four named outcomes with explicit requirements stop the drift into the informal fifth option of shipping and hoping
pros.example: a bracelet with a bare link interior being routed to rework rather than polished at the edges and boxed

pros.claim: Requiring the verification verdict for release keeps appearance from standing in for proof
pros.example: declining to release a bright, beautiful cuff whose recess thickness was never checked after a coverage complaint

cons.claim: The strict release condition slows delivery on jobs where measurement capacity is the bottleneck
cons.example: a wedding deadline waiting on a measurement slot for a piece that looks perfect

cons.claim: Disclosure-based release depends on the customer understanding a technical trade-off in a short conversation
cons.example: explaining why a flash-class refresh on a worn ring will not wear like the original before they accept it

failure_modes: releasing on appearance while the deposit verification is still open
choosing rework because it feels generous, on a piece that stripping is likely to destroy
deciding a label-relevant consequence at the bench instead of flagging it for verification
acceptance_tests: every disposition entry names the outcome, the evidence behind it and the verification verdict it relies on
any disposition touching a label-relevant property carries a compliance flag rather than a bench decision
revisit_triggers: a released or disclosed piece returns with the same defect
the verification lane revises its verdict after the disposition was made

base.update_signal: a disposition is reversed by a return, a measurement revision or a compliance finding

nodes.definition: Before rework is offered, the piece is assessed for whether stripping is survivable at all, because chemical or electrolytic stripping does not politely remove only the failed gold. The assessment walks the construction: set stones and their settings, since many stones and most glues, resins, pearls and organics do not tolerate stripping chemistry or the heat and ultrasonics that go with it; soldered joints, where a filler of different composition can be attacked faster than the parent metal; hollow, filled or laminated bodies, where solution enters and cannot be rinsed out and later bleeds and stains; plated-on-plated history, where an unknown intermediate layer determines what the stripper will actually attack; thin or worn base metal on a piece that has already been polished several times over its life, where losing more material means losing the piece; and silver or other soft bases where stripping removes base along with deposit and can carry the article out of the class it was sold under. The output is a plain statement — strippable, strippable with named risks, or not strippable — and it is made before any promise is given to the customer, never after the piece is already in a beaker.

included: construction review for stones, solder, hollows, prior plating and worn base
the three-way strippable verdict with named risks
flagging base-metal loss that could disturb a label class
excluded: selecting or operating the stripping chemistry, which the safety and waste unit governs
gemstone identification and jewellery repair work, which the bench-repair trade owns
approving the rework, which the approval gate owns

pros.claim: Assessing before promising prevents the worst outcome in this subdomain, which is destroying goods while trying to help
pros.example: stopping at a glued half-drilled pearl earring instead of learning about the glue in the stripper

pros.claim: Naming the risks converts a vague worry into something a customer can decide about
pros.example: telling the owner of a thin, much-polished shank that stripping will remove more metal from an already worn band

cons.claim: The construction of an unfamiliar piece cannot always be known, so the verdict carries residual uncertainty
cons.example: a vintage locket whose interior construction and prior repairs are invisible from outside

cons.claim: A cautious verdict loses work the shop could technically have done
cons.example: declining a stone-set rework that a specialist bench would have unset, stripped and reset routinely

failure_modes: assessing after the customer has already been promised a perfect result
treating a stone-set or hollow piece as ordinary because the last one happened to survive
ignoring that stripping a silver-based article removes base metal and can disturb what the piece was sold as
acceptance_tests: every rework case carries a written strippable, strippable-with-risks or not-strippable verdict with the construction observations behind it
the verdict exists before any customer-facing rework promise and before any chemistry is prepared
revisit_triggers: a piece behaves unexpectedly in stripping, indicating the construction review missed something
a new stripping product or method changes what is survivable

base.update_signal: a stripped piece is damaged in a way the construction review did not anticipate

nodes.definition: Rework on goods the shop does not own is a decision for their owner, and this gate makes that explicit and recorded. Before a customer's piece meets stripper, the customer is told in writing what is proposed and what it costs them beyond money: that stripping removes the existing deposit and unavoidably takes some base metal with it, that engraving, hallmarks, patina and fine detail can soften, that stones, glues, pearls and hollow constructions carry the named risks the feasibility verdict identified, that the result is a second plating rather than the original factory finish, and that in the worst case the piece may be damaged or lost. The record names who approved, when, on what description, and what the agreed outcome is if the piece does not survive. Two boundaries sit on this gate: where the rework would disturb a label-relevant property the case is flagged for compliance verification in the selling jurisdiction before approval is sought, and where the shop cannot meet the stripping safety obligation classes the answer is no regardless of what the customer is willing to accept.

included: what must be disclosed before approval
the content and retention of the approval record
the compliance flag and the safety veto on the gate
excluded: pricing and refund terms
approving a regulated label claim
the stripping operation itself

pros.claim: A written approval converts the highest-risk step in the subdomain into a shared, informed decision
pros.example: an heirloom owner choosing to accept a slightly softened engraving rather than keep a peeling finish, on record

pros.claim: The gate forces the risk conversation early, when the customer still has other options
pros.example: a customer choosing a return and a refund instead of a rework once the metal-loss risk is explained

cons.claim: The disclosure can frighten a customer away from a rework that was genuinely low risk
cons.example: a plain silver band owner declining a routine strip because the standard risk list sounds alarming

cons.claim: Written approval takes time that a walk-in repair counter does not always have
cons.example: a customer waiting while the risk description is written for a same-day job

failure_modes: starting a strip on a verbal 'just make it right' with nothing recorded
disclosing only the cosmetic risks and not the loss-of-piece and detail-softening risks
seeking approval for a rework whose safety obligations the shop cannot actually meet
acceptance_tests: no customer piece enters stripping chemistry without a retained approval record naming the risks, the approver and the date
any rework that would disturb a label-relevant property carries a compliance verification flag raised before approval was sought
revisit_triggers: a customer disputes what they approved
a rework outcome falls outside what the disclosure described

base.update_signal: a dispute or a damaged-piece outcome shows the disclosure did not cover a real risk

nodes.definition: Stripping is plating's equal in hazard and is treated as such. Commercial strippers arrive as cyanide-class electrolytic products, as strong acid or oxidizer blends, and as proprietary selective formulations, and each is used only per its own technical data sheet with the training the product and the jurisdiction require; nothing is improvised, mixed or 'strengthened' at the bench. The obligation classes are the same ones the plating room runs on: segregation of incompatible chemistries in use and in storage, labeled and secured containers, dedicated tools and trays, PPE appropriate to the class, ventilation or extraction over the working position, documented training before first use, and emergency readiness including eyewash, spill provision and a plan the operator has actually rehearsed. One line is absolute and applies to diagnosis and rework alike: cyanide-class solutions and acids are never mixed, never stored together and never share a drain, because that combination generates a rapidly lethal gas. Waste is part of the operation rather than an afterthought — spent strip solutions carry dissolved gold with real value and hazardous constituents with real liability, so they go to a licensed reclaim or disposal route, never down a sink, and the discharge and hazardous-waste rules that apply are the ones in force in your jurisdiction, which are verified before the first strip rather than after an inspection.

included: stripper product classes used per TDS with required training
the obligation classes of segregation, storage, labeling, PPE, ventilation, training and emergency readiness
the cyanide-and-acid hard line covering use, storage and drains
gold-bearing waste routed to licensed reclaim with jurisdiction rules verified
excluded: formulating stripping chemistry from raw chemicals
prescribing a specific concentration, temperature or immersion time, which the product data sheet governs
interpreting a specific jurisdiction's regulation text, which is verified with the authority or a competent adviser

pros.claim: Treating stripping as plating-grade hazard closes the most common gap in a small shop's safety thinking
pros.example: a bench that ventilates and segregates its plating line but keeps a stripper jar next to the pickle pot until this rule is applied

pros.claim: Routing spent strip solution to licensed reclaim recovers real value while discharging a real obligation
pros.example: accumulating gold-bearing strip solution for the refiner instead of pouring away both the metal and the compliance

cons.claim: Meeting the obligation classes may exceed what a small bench can provide, which removes in-house rework as an option
cons.example: a shop without extraction deciding it cannot strip in-house and sending rework out instead

cons.claim: Licensed waste routes and training cost money and calendar time before any rework revenue exists
cons.example: waiting for a scheduled training session and a waste-collection agreement before the first strip job

failure_modes: storing or draining a cyanide-class stripper anywhere near acids, which is the fatal-outcome failure of this subdomain
improvising a stronger or hotter strip than the product data sheet describes to save time
sinking spent strip solution, losing both the recoverable gold and the legal position
acceptance_tests: each stripping product in use has its data sheet on file, its own labeled storage away from incompatible classes, and a trained named operator
spent strip solutions and rinses are collected to a documented reclaim or licensed disposal route with the applicable jurisdiction rules recorded as verified
revisit_triggers: a new stripping product, supplier or revised data sheet enters the shop
the workspace, ventilation, drainage or waste contractor changes
a near miss, spill or exposure event occurs

base.update_signal: a product data sheet revision, a jurisdiction rule change or a near-miss event

nodes.definition: A replate is a new job, not a touch-up, and treating it otherwise is how a shop makes the same defect twice on the same piece. After stripping, the piece is inspected bare, because stripping reveals what the first deposit was hiding: scratches, porosity, seams, worn areas and prior repairs that must be dealt with mechanically before any chemistry, and that sometimes change the disposition entirely. The full prep chain is then run as specified for that substrate rather than abbreviated because the piece 'was only just plated', and the routed cause is confirmed corrected before the piece goes in — a new rack position or contact if racking was the cause, the analysed and corrected bath if chemistry was, the restored cleaning or strike discipline if prep was. The replate is documented as its own run with its own logbook row, its own witness coupon and its own retained photographs, cross-referenced to the original job and to the diagnosis, so that if it fails again the pair can be compared. Nothing is plated over a failed deposit: adhesion failures in particular reproduce faithfully through any layer laid on top of them.

included: bare-piece inspection after stripping and its consequences
full prep chain rather than an abbreviated one
confirming the routed correction before the replate
documenting the replate as its own cross-referenced run
excluded: performing the prep steps and the plating run, which the prep and process lanes execute
specifying thickness class for the replate, which the verification sibling owns
re-negotiating the job scope with the customer

pros.claim: Inspecting the bare piece catches substrate problems the first deposit concealed, before more money is spent
pros.example: finding a porous casting face under the stripped gold and changing the plan from replate to a documented conversation

pros.claim: Requiring the correction to be confirmed first stops the shop from paying twice for the same defect
pros.example: holding the replate until the rack with the tired contact fingers has actually been repaired

cons.claim: A full prep chain on a rework costs as much as a new job while earning less or nothing
cons.example: a warranty replate consuming a full cycle of bench time on a piece already paid for once

cons.claim: Bare inspection can reveal problems that leave the piece in a worse negotiating position than before the strip
cons.example: discovering wear-through at a shank only after the deposit is gone and the customer is waiting

failure_modes: plating over a partially stripped or lifting deposit to save a step
abbreviating the prep chain because the piece looks clean after stripping
running the replate before the routed lane has confirmed its correction, which wastes the piece and the evidence
acceptance_tests: the replate has its own logbook row, witness coupon and photographs, cross-referenced to the original job and the diagnosis entry
the routed correction is recorded as confirmed before the replate run starts
revisit_triggers: the replate shows the same defect class as the original run
bare inspection reveals substrate conditions that change the disposition

base.update_signal: a replate reproduces the original defect, or bare inspection routinely reveals conditions the diagnosis missed

nodes.definition: What the customer is told is part of the work, not a postscript, and this unit fixes both the content and the limits of that conversation. The content is plain: what was found, what the evidence says about why, what was or will be done, and what the piece is when it comes back — including that it is a re-plated finish rather than the original, and that plated goods are plated goods and are never described as solid gold. The limits are firm. Durability is expressed as a measured result where the verification lane has measured it, or as an estimate that names the method and its uncertainty where it has not, and never as a wear-life promise invented to settle a complaint.
