Regulated terms such as gold plated, gold flashed, vermeil, gold filled and rolled gold, and any fineness or nickel-release statement, are compliance classes tied to the selling jurisdiction; where a defect or a rework touches one, the customer is told that the claim is being verified rather than being given a new claim on the spot. Where a piece has heirloom or sentimental value, the risk of any further intervention is stated before it is undertaken, and an honest 'this is as good as this stack will get' is treated as a legitimate professional answer.

included: what is disclosed about findings, cause, action and the returned piece
durability language backed by measurement or method-named estimate
regulated terms treated as compliance classes to verify
heirloom risk stated before intervention
excluded: approving a label or compliance claim
legal, medical or financial advice, including allergy guidance beyond routing to regulation classes and professional care
commercial negotiation and warranty terms

pros.claim: Plain disclosure of what a re-plated finish is prevents the second complaint that follows an oversold repair
pros.example: saying up front that a refreshed worn ring will wear again at the same rate rather than implying it is now permanent

pros.claim: Method-named estimates let the shop answer durability questions honestly instead of going silent or inventing a number
pros.example: describing a thickness class as measured on a ride-along coupon and explaining what that method does and does not cover

cons.claim: Honest uncertainty reads as evasiveness to a customer who wanted a simple guarantee
cons.example: a buyer who wanted 'how many years' hearing a wear-class explanation instead

cons.claim: Refusing to restate a label term on the spot can stall a sale or an exchange
cons.example: declining to confirm that a stripped and replated silver piece still meets its original label class until the rules are verified

failure_modes: offering a wear-life figure to calm an upset customer
describing plated goods as solid gold or letting a customer's wrong assumption stand uncorrected
restating or upgrading a regulated label term at the counter instead of flagging it for verification
acceptance_tests: no customer-facing statement in the case file contains a durability figure that is neither measured nor labeled as a method-named estimate
every case touching a regulated term records that the claim was referred for verification rather than answered at the counter
revisit_triggers: a customer reports understanding something the shop did not intend to promise
a jurisdiction's labeling or nickel-release rules are updated

base.update_signal: a complaint, dispute or rule change shows the disclosure language was misleading or outdated

nodes.definition: A single defect is an incident; the log is what turns incidents into knowledge. Each case gets one entry containing the defect class and photographs, the three axis answers, the witness and retained-part comparison, the discriminating test and its result, the confirmed or most-likely cause with its confidence stated honestly, the lane it was routed to, the change that lane made, the disposition, and the outcome. Entries are then counted and sorted, because the shape of the log answers questions no single case can: which defect class dominates, which lane owns most of the causes, whether failures cluster on a product family, an operator, a rack, a shift, a substrate or a period in the bath's life, and whether the rate is rising. The log is also the memory that survives staff turnover and the evidence base if a customer or an insurer disputes what happened. Its discipline is unglamorous and it is the first thing abandoned under pressure, which is exactly why the workflow closes a case only when the entry is complete rather than when the piece is out the door.

included: the required contents of a defect log entry
counting and sorting to find dominant classes, lanes and clusters
the log as dispute evidence and as institutional memory
excluded: batch process records and measurement records, which the run log and the verification sibling own
statistical process control methods beyond simple counting and clustering
personnel evaluation based on defect counts

pros.claim: Counting classes reveals the systemic cause that individually reasonable case-by-case fixes keep missing
pros.example: eight blister cases in a quarter all traced to the same shift-change transfer delay once they are counted together

pros.claim: A complete entry lets a later dispute be answered with evidence rather than with recollection
pros.example: showing a customer the dated photographs and the coupon result from the original run a year later

cons.claim: Log discipline competes directly with bench time and is the first casualty of a busy week
cons.example: three cases closed verbally during a holiday rush and never written up

cons.claim: Small shops have small numbers, so trends are noisy and can suggest patterns that are not there
cons.example: two pitting cases in one week on unrelated jobs reading as an outbreak

failure_modes: closing a case when the piece ships rather than when the entry is complete
recording the disposition but not the cause and the lane change, which destroys trending
using defect counts to blame an individual, which reliably stops honest reporting
acceptance_tests: every closed case has an entry containing class, axis answers, comparison result, cause with stated confidence, lane, change made, disposition and outcome
the log is reviewed on a defined cadence with the class and lane counts written down
revisit_triggers: a review shows entries missing the cause or the lane outcome
a defect class or a cluster crosses whatever threshold the shop set for action

base.update_signal: a trend review changes which defect class or lane the shop treats as its main problem

nodes.definition: A diagnosis that ends with a corrected piece has done half its job; the other half is making the same defect less likely next time and proving that it worked. Each closed case must name one prevention change and the artifact it lives in, so that the learning outlives the memory of the case: a step added to the run checklist, a gate moved earlier in the sequence, a new acceptance check on the release list, a fixture or rack modification, a written trigger such as treating visible hue drift as a reason to schedule analysis before the next batch, a change in what is retained per run, or a training point for whoever runs the step. The change is then verified rather than assumed: a recurrence check is scheduled over a named number of subsequent runs or a named period, and the case is only marked closed when that window passes without the class reappearing. If it does reappear, the earlier cause is demoted from confirmed to unconfirmed and the case reopens at the evidence triad rather than continuing to build on a conclusion that has now failed twice. This loop is what stops a shop from re-learning the same lesson every year.

included: naming one prevention change per closed case and where it lives
the scheduled recurrence check and the closure rule
demoting a failed cause and reopening at the evidence triad
excluded: implementing the change inside another lane's procedure, which that lane owns
certification, audit or formal quality-system administration
measuring the corrected deposit, which the verification sibling performs

pros.claim: One named change per case makes improvement concrete and auditable instead of aspirational
pros.example: a case closing with the water-break check moved to a signed line on the run sheet rather than with a resolution to be careful

pros.claim: The recurrence window converts hope into evidence that the fix held
pros.example: six subsequent runs inspected specifically for blisters before the adhesion case is finally closed

cons.claim: Checklists accumulate faster than they are pruned, and an overloaded procedure gets skipped wholesale
cons.example: a run sheet grown to two pages of checks that operators start signing without reading

cons.claim: Recurrence windows delay closure and tie up attention on cases everyone believes are finished
cons.example: a case held open for weeks while the shop waits for enough runs of that product family

failure_modes: closing a case with a general intention rather than a change written into an artifact
declaring victory after one clean batch without a defined recurrence window
letting a failed prevention change stand as though the cause were still confirmed
acceptance_tests: each closed case names one prevention change, the artifact it was written into, and the recurrence window that must pass before closure
any recurrence within the window reopens the case at the evidence triad and demotes the earlier cause to unconfirmed
revisit_triggers: a defect class recurs after its prevention change
the run sheet or checklist grows to the point where operators start skipping items

base.update_signal: a prevention change fails its recurrence window or a checklist audit shows items being skipped

edges.why_related: a defect can only be classed against the library from the photographs and the unaltered piece that intake preserved
the location, timing and tank axes are answered from the intake record's photographs, identifiers and history
the attribution rule sets what counts as an acceptable answer on each axis before the axes are read
the replay is aimed by the axis answers: which run to reconstruct and which comparison actually discriminates
the replay supplies the baseline and the surviving candidate causes that the one-variable experiment is built to separate
whether the lifting is whole-surface or localized, and whether it appeared at unracking or in service, selects the branch of the adhesion tree
burn is diagnosed almost entirely from where on the geometry and which rack positions it appears, which the axes supply
haze is only a bath-aging question once the coupon and the retained-part trend show it is load-wide and progressive
thin-versus-bare and its position on the piece are axis answers before they are causes
a hue deviation must be separated from haze, thin coverage and staining by class before any cause family is assigned
the same-load control that a substrate claim requires is itself a designed one-variable test
an interface finding is only actionable once it is routed to the prep, chemistry or process lane that owns it
current, distribution and contact causes belong to the process lane and bath-supply causes to chemistry, which routing decides
bath aging and contamination hypotheses can only be settled by the chemistry lane's analysis, so they are routed rather than acted on
fixture, mask, contact and current-distribution corrections are process-lane work handed over with the coverage evidence
what happens to the affected goods depends on what the cause was and whether its lane can correct it before delivery
the feasibility review is only entered once rework is the candidate disposition, and it can send the decision back to return
the risks disclosed for approval are exactly the ones the construction review identified
no stripping chemistry is prepared for customer goods until the documented approval exists
the replate begins from the bare, rinsed piece the controlled stripping operation produced
what must be said to the customer follows from which of the four outcomes was chosen
the log entry is built from the routing record: cause, lane, requested change and outcome
prevention changes are chosen from what the counted log says dominates, not from the most recent complaint
a shop that cannot meet the segregation, ventilation, training and waste obligation classes has no in-house rework option, which removes a disposition from the menu
the approval record bounds what the replate may do to the piece, including how much detail softening and metal loss was accepted
release-with-disclosure is only available if the disclosure can be made truthfully without inventing a durability or label claim
the substrate lane may not be used as a destination until its proof standard is met, which constrains where a cause may be routed
the same load can burn at the edges and starve in the recesses, and the obvious single lever of current moves both defects in opposite directions
edges.resolution_rule: fix distribution first (thieving, shielding, spacing, hanging orientation, agitation) before moving current; if a current change is unavoidable, protect against burn, since a burnt deposit is scrap while a thin recess can be measured, disclosed or re-run

edges.why_related: confirming a cause properly takes runs and hours that a promised delivery date does not have, and the pressure is to decide the goods first and diagnose later
edges.resolution_rule: the disposition of the affected goods may proceed on the evidence in hand, but the cause is recorded as unconfirmed and the batch behind it stays quarantined until the discriminating test is run; a deadline never converts an unconfirmed cause into a confirmed one in the log

edges.why_related: rework is the disposition that most satisfies everyone, and it is also the one that can destroy the customer's piece outright
edges.resolution_rule: when the feasibility verdict is not-strippable, or strippable-with-risks that the customer has not accepted in writing, the disposition falls back to return or release-with-disclosure; the irreversible option never wins on goodwill alone

edges.why_related: the substrate explanation is always available, always comfortable for the shop, and sometimes true, which is precisely why it competes with the no-blame default
edges.resolution_rule: the no-blame default holds until all three bars are met (clean same-load control, defect follows the piece across a re-run, named observation on the piece); until then the shop-controlled lanes stay open and the customer hears a hypothesis, not a verdict

edges.why_related: pores through the deposit over a less noble base produce the late-appearing spots that present as staining weeks later, so one tree's defect becomes the other's symptom

an adhesion finding forces full removal rather than an overplate, because any layer laid on a lifting deposit reproduces the failure, so the feasibility question is raised by the adhesion diagnosis itself
the retained part and the witness coupon are pulled and protected at intake, before any destructive test consumes the only comparison available
the log entry is completed after the disposition is made and the outcome is known, and the case is not closed before that
defects the shop actually saw, with their photographs, are what keeps the class library current as products and stacks change
the counted history tells the bench which axis question discriminates fastest for this shop's recurring classes, sharpening the next diagnosis
both read whole-load, bath-origin symptoms with the same coupon-and-trend discriminator, and both end as referrals for analysis rather than bench corrections

conflict_axes.name: evidence_discipline_vs_pattern_recognition_speed
conflict_axes.description: An experienced plater recognizes a defect in a second and is usually right, but the diagnosis that skips the axes is the one that misses the case where the familiar pattern has an unfamiliar cause.
poles: act on the experienced eye immediately
answer the three axes before naming any cause
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the experienced guess be written down as the prediction, then require the axes and the witness comparison to confirm or refute it before it is routed

conflict_axes.name: rework_generosity_vs_piece_survival
conflict_axes.description: Stripping and replating feels like the generous answer to a complaint, and it is also the only step in this subdomain that can destroy the customer's goods outright.
poles: protect the piece from an irreversible process
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: feasibility verdict first, documented approval naming the risks second, and return or disclosure whenever the risk is material and unaccepted

conflict_axes.name: throughput_pressure_vs_confirmed_cause
conflict_axes.description: Deadlines want the goods dispositioned and the line running again, while a confirmed cause needs coupons, a re-run and time that the schedule has already spent.
poles: ship the batch and move on
hold until the cause is confirmed
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: separate the two decisions: disposition the goods on the evidence in hand, keep the rest of the batch quarantined, and keep the cause labeled unconfirmed until the test is run

conflict_axes.name: safety_obligation_vs_speed_of_rework
conflict_axes.description: A quick dip in stripper is the fastest way to make a complaint disappear and the most direct route to the one accident this trade cannot recover from.
poles: strip it now and get it back to the customer
meet every obligation class before any stripping
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: safety and compliance dominate absolutely: no segregation, ventilation, training, PPE, emergency readiness and waste route means no in-house stripping, whatever the deadline or the customer's willingness

conflict_axes.name: single_piece_fix_vs_systemic_cause
conflict_axes.description: Fixing the returned piece satisfies the customer in front of you, while the same cause is quietly producing the next three complaints in the batch behind it.
poles: stop the cause across the shop
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: quarantine the batch and route the cause before the individual rework, and treat a repeat class in the log as a systemic case even when each instance was individually resolved

conflict_axes.name: cosmetic_tolerance_vs_functional_failure
conflict_axes.description: The visible defect and the serious defect are often different defects: a small blemish irritates the customer while an invisible pore over a steel core is the one that will rust.
poles: prioritize what the customer can see
prioritize what will fail in service
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: grade every defect on both axes and let the functional grade drive the disposition while the cosmetic grade drives the conversation

conflict_axes.name: honest_disclosure_vs_customer_reassurance
conflict_axes.description: The upset customer wants a number and a promise, and the only honest answers available are a measured result, a method-named estimate or a compliance class that must be verified.
poles: state only what is measured or honestly estimated
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: honesty dominates: describe the method behind any durability statement, never invent wear life, never restate a regulated label term at the counter, and treat 'this is as good as this stack gets' as a legitimate answer

conflict_axes.name: shop_fault_default_vs_substrate_attribution
conflict_axes.description: Every defect has a comfortable explanation in the customer's goods and an uncomfortable one in the shop's own process, and the comfortable one ends the investigation early.
poles: assume the incoming piece was the problem
assume a shop-controlled cause until proven otherwise
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: no-blame default holds until the same-load control, the follow-the-piece re-run and a named observation on the piece all support the substrate class

conflict_axes.name: bench_screen_vs_instrumented_evidence
conflict_axes.description: Cheap in-house screens catch process drift and settle most cases, while a disputed claim, a compliance question or an insurance conversation needs measurement and method the bench cannot supply.
poles: decide it with the loupe and the coupon
escalate to instrumented or accredited evidence
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use bench screens for process control and routing, and escalate to the verification lane or a send-out class whenever a claim, a compliance class or a dispute depends on the number

edge_cases.description: An inherited piece of unknown construction comes back peeling; it carries soft solder seams, an unidentified prior coating and no documentation of what it is
edge_cases.trigger: a rework request on an antique or inherited article with unknown metallurgy and history
edge_cases.mitigation: treat construction as unknown rather than assumed, run a control and a discreet test area where possible, state the unknowns explicitly in the approval record, and prefer return over an irreversible process on an irreplaceable piece

edge_cases.description: A stone-set ring needs stripping, but the setting holds a heat-sensitive or porous stone and the shop cannot tell whether the stone is glued
edge_cases.trigger: rework proposed on goods with set stones, pearls, resins or organics
edge_cases.mitigation: verdict is not-strippable as presented; options are unsetting by a competent bench first, a masked partial approach where the construction allows it, or return with disclosure — never an exploratory dip

edge_cases.description: A piece plates and ships perfectly, then returns after two weeks of wear with dark points and a rust bloom at a wear edge
edge_cases.trigger: a field failure appearing only after service, when the run evidence has gone cold
edge_cases.mitigation: reconstruct from the retained part and coupon of that run rather than from the returned piece alone, screen the retained part for porosity on aged deposit, and treat the case as a class-level question about the stack rather than a one-piece complaint

edge_cases.description: Only the two outermost positions on the rack show burn, and every other piece in the same load is perfect
edge_cases.trigger: a defect that correlates with rack position rather than with piece or bath
edge_cases.mitigation: record the position map before unracking, route to the process lane as a distribution and fixturing case, and explicitly close the bath hypothesis in the log so nobody doses a healthy tank

edge_cases.description: The witness coupon comes out flawless while the customer's piece is defective, and the shop wants to conclude the piece was at fault
edge_cases.trigger: a clean coupon beside a defective part on the same run
edge_cases.mitigation: treat a clean coupon as evidence of part-local cause, not of substrate fault: geometry, racking, masking and handling are part-local too, and the substrate proof standard still has to be met before the piece is named

edge_cases.description: The customer polishes, dips or otherwise cleans the defective piece before returning it, removing the film, the smut and the blister edge
edge_cases.trigger: a returned piece that has been altered before intake
edge_cases.mitigation: record the alteration in the intake record, downgrade every conclusion that depended on the destroyed evidence to unconfirmed, and rebuild the case from the retained part, the coupon and the run log instead

edge_cases.description: A hollow bangle or filled bead is stripped and later bleeds solution from an interior cavity, staining the new deposit days after delivery
edge_cases.trigger: stripping or plating a hollow, filled or laminated construction that cannot be fully rinsed
edge_cases.mitigation: identify hollow and filled construction at feasibility, treat entrapment as a named risk in the approval record, and where the cavity cannot be verified as clear treat the piece as not-strippable rather than gambling on the rinse

edge_cases.description: A stripped silver-based piece loses enough base metal and deposit that its original selling description may no longer hold
edge_cases.trigger: a rework that changes a property tied to a regulated label class
edge_cases.mitigation: raise the compliance flag before approval is sought, tell the customer the claim is being verified against current rules in the selling jurisdiction rather than restated at the counter, and route the claim question out of this lane entirely

edge_cases.description: A single piece shows two defect classes at once, such as a hazy surface that is also blistered along a seam, and the log records only the more visible one
edge_cases.trigger: co-occurring defects with different causes on the same article
edge_cases.mitigation: record every class present in evidence order, run the trees separately, and route a primary and a secondary lane with the observation that would separate them rather than forcing one story

edge_cases.description: The same defect class reappears three runs after a prevention change that everyone believed had fixed it
edge_cases.trigger: recurrence inside the scheduled recurrence window
edge_cases.mitigation: demote the earlier cause from confirmed to unconfirmed, reopen at the evidence triad with both runs' evidence side by side, and treat the failed prevention change itself as a data point rather than repeating it harder

edge_cases.description: A cramped bench has the stripping jar, the pickle pot and a single drain within arm's reach of each other
edge_cases.trigger: any stripping operation in a workspace without physical segregation of incompatible chemistries
edge_cases.mitigation: stop: cyanide-class solutions and acids are never mixed, never stored together and never share a drain; either establish segregated storage, working zones, tools and waste routes with the jurisdiction's rules verified, or remove in-house stripping from the disposition menu and send rework out

edge_cases.description: A batch already delivered is implicated by a diagnosis made on a later return from the same run
edge_cases.trigger: a systemic cause confirmed after some of the affected goods have shipped
edge_cases.mitigation: identify the affected jobs from the run log, decide a proactive disclosure with an inspection or rework offer rather than waiting for complaints, and record the decision and its reasoning in the log

workflow.action: Quarantine the piece and capture it as evidence
workflow.description: Isolate the piece and its batch, photograph the defect and a good zone before any handling, and recover job, run, rack and history identifiers
workflow.artifact: defect intake record with dated photographs and run identifiers
workflow.gate: the piece is unaltered and quarantined, the batch is held, and the run it came from is identified

workflow.action: Name the defect against the class library
workflow.description: Assign one or more named classes by comparing against the retained photo library rather than using an informal word
workflow.artifact: defect class assignment with library reference images
workflow.gate: every class present on the piece is named from the library, in evidence order

workflow.description: Record where on the piece, when in the run and the calendar, and which tank or step the pattern points at, marking any axis that cannot be answered as unknown
workflow.artifact: diagnosis sheet with the three axis answers
workflow.gate: all three axes are answered or explicitly marked unknown, and at least one candidate cause is eliminated by an axis answer

workflow.action: Replay the run against witness, retained part and log
workflow.description: Compare the ride-along coupon, the retained part and the neighbouring runs to split bath-wide from part-local and to date the onset
workflow.gate: the bath-wide versus part-local call is stated with the comparison that supports it

workflow.action: Walk the cause tree for the named class
workflow.description: Work the branch structure of the matching tree — adhesion, burn, haze, pitting, staining, coverage or color — and list the candidate causes that survive the evidence
workflow.artifact: ranked candidate causes with the evidence for and against each
workflow.gate: each surviving candidate is consistent with all three axis answers and the replay result

workflow.action: Design and run the discriminating test
workflow.description: Write the prediction, change one variable, run it on coupons or scrap of the same stack, and inspect it the same way the defect was inspected
workflow.artifact: test record with prediction, single variable and observed result
workflow.gate: the test ran on coupons rather than customer goods, changed one variable, and either confirms a cause or triggers the stop rule

workflow.action: Route the cause to the lane that owns it
workflow.description: Assign a single primary lane — prep, chemistry, process or the evidenced substrate boundary — and hand over the evidence pack with the one change requested
workflow.artifact: lane handover pack with the requested change
workflow.gate: one primary lane is named, the requested change is specific, and the case stays open until the lane reports back

workflow.action: Decide the disposition of the affected goods
workflow.description: Choose release, release with disclosure, rework or return against the stated requirement for each, with the verification verdict in hand
workflow.artifact: disposition record with the evidence and verification verdict cited
workflow.gate: release is supported by the verification verdict, and any label-relevant consequence carries a compliance flag instead of a bench decision

workflow.action: Assess strip feasibility and obtain documented approval
workflow.description: Review the construction for stones, solder, hollows, prior plating and worn base, then disclose the named risks and record the customer's decision before any chemistry is prepared
workflow.artifact: feasibility verdict plus retained rework approval record
workflow.gate: a written approval naming the risks, the approver and the date exists before stripping, and the safety obligations are confirmed achievable

workflow.action: Strip under the obligation classes and route the waste
workflow.description: Use the commercial stripper per its data sheet with trained personnel, segregated storage and working zones, ventilation and PPE, and collect the gold-bearing spent solution for licensed reclaim
workflow.artifact: stripping run record with product, operator, controls and waste routing
workflow.gate: segregation, ventilation, PPE, training and emergency readiness are in place, cyanide-class and acid chemistries share no storage or drain, and the waste route is documented

workflow.action: Replate as a new job from a full prep chain
workflow.description: Inspect the bare piece, run the full prep chain for that substrate, and confirm the routed correction is in place before the piece goes in
workflow.artifact: replate run record with its own logbook row, coupon and photographs cross-referenced to the original
workflow.gate: the routed correction is recorded as confirmed and nothing has been plated over a failed deposit

workflow.action: Log the case and close the prevention loop
workflow.description: Complete the log entry, name one prevention change and the artifact it lives in, and schedule the recurrence check that must pass before closure
workflow.artifact: completed defect log entry with prevention change and recurrence window
workflow.gate: the entry is complete, one prevention change is written into a named artifact, and the recurrence window is scheduled

dominance_rules.rule: Safety and compliance obligation classes dominate every rework and diagnosis decision
dominance_rules.rationale: a stripping or handling accident, above all any contact between cyanide-class solutions and acids, is the one failure in this trade that cannot be reworked afterwards
dominance_rules.trigger: any step that would prepare, use, store or dispose of stripping or test chemistry
dominance_rules.action: verify segregation, storage, labeling, PPE, ventilation, training, emergency readiness and the waste route against the product data sheet and the jurisdiction's rules; if any is missing, the step does not happen in-house at any price or deadline

dominance_rules.rule: Documented customer approval dominates shop convenience on customer goods
dominance_rules.rationale: stripping and replating consume base metal and detail that belong to the owner, not to the shop
dominance_rules.trigger: a rework proposed on any article the shop does not own
dominance_rules.action: obtain and retain a written approval naming the metal-loss, detail-softening, construction and loss-of-piece risks before any chemistry touches the piece

dominance_rules.rule: Evidence dominates familiarity when they disagree
dominance_rules.rationale: the shop's most familiar cause is the one it will find whether or not it is there, which is how a real cause survives for months
dominance_rules.trigger: the three axis answers or the witness comparison contradict the first hypothesis
dominance_rules.action: keep the evidence-consistent candidates, record the familiar hypothesis as refuted with the observation that refuted it, and design the test around what remains

dominance_rules.rule: The no-blame default dominates the substrate explanation until its proof standard is met
dominance_rules.rationale: defaulting to the customer's goods ends the investigation exactly where the shop's own repeatable cause lives, and costs the customer as well
dominance_rules.trigger: a substrate limitation is proposed as the cause
dominance_rules.action: require a clean same-load control, a defect that follows the piece across a re-run and a named observation on the piece; until all three exist, keep the shop-controlled lanes open and speak in hypotheses

dominance_rules.rule: Functional failure dominates cosmetic appearance in setting the disposition
dominance_rules.rationale: an invisible pore over a corroding base will fail in service while a visible blemish only disappoints, and the disposition must follow the failure that matters
dominance_rules.trigger: a piece grades differently on cosmetic and functional severity
dominance_rules.action: let the functional grade select release, rework or return, and let the cosmetic grade shape the conversation rather than the decision

dominance_rules.rule: Verification evidence dominates appearance for any release
dominance_rules.rationale: a beautiful surface says nothing about thickness, adhesion or porosity, and release without the verification verdict is a claim the shop cannot support
dominance_rules.trigger: a piece that looks acceptable after a defect investigation is proposed for release
dominance_rules.action: release only with the verification lane's verdict in hand; otherwise hold, or move to release-with-disclosure of exactly what is and is not known

dominance_rules.rationale: the shop can re-run a thin recess but cannot un-strip a destroyed heirloom
dominance_rules.trigger: the feasibility verdict is not-strippable or strippable-with-material-risks that the customer has not accepted in writing
dominance_rules.action: fall back to return or release-with-disclosure and record why the irreversible path was declined

dominance_rules.rule: Systemic cause dominates the single-piece fix once a class repeats
dominance_rules.rationale: individually resolving each instance of a repeating class pays for the same defect over and over while it keeps shipping
dominance_rules.trigger: the same defect class appears again within the shop's defined review window
dominance_rules.action: quarantine the affected production, escalate to a systemic case in the log, and treat the earlier per-piece resolutions as unconfirmed

dominance_rules.rationale: an invented durability figure or a counter-restated label term converts a quality problem into a misrepresentation problem
dominance_rules.trigger: a customer asks how long it will last, what it is now, or whether the piece can still be described as it was sold
dominance_rules.action: answer with measured results or method-named estimates, never describe plated goods as solid gold, and refer any regulated label or fineness question for verification against current rules in the selling jurisdiction

anti_rework_rules.rule: Photograph and quarantine before anything is cleaned, polished or re-dipped
anti_rework_rules.prevents: destroying the interface, film and pattern evidence that every later cause tree depends on, leaving a diagnosis that can never be closed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the defect class before proposing a cause
anti_rework_rules.prevents: walking the wrong cause tree for a week and routing a lane that could never have produced this defect

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pull the retained part and the witness coupon before any destructive test
anti_rework_rules.prevents: consuming the only comparison that could have separated a bath-wide cause from a part-local one

anti_rework_rules.rule: Answer the three axes before touching a tank control or a bath addition
anti_rework_rules.prevents: correcting a healthy bath for a racking or fixture defect, which adds a chemistry problem on top of the original one

anti_rework_rules.rule: Assess strippability before promising a rework to the customer
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an approval given for a process that will damage or destroy the piece, and the unwinnable conversation that follows

anti_rework_rules.rule: Obtain the documented approval before any stripper is prepared
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an irreversible intervention on goods whose owner never agreed to the risks, with no record of what was disclosed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the routed correction is in place before the replate goes in
anti_rework_rules.prevents: producing the identical defect a second time on the same piece, at the shop's cost and with the customer watching

anti_rework_rules.rule: Never plate over a failed deposit; strip to bare and run the full prep chain
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an adhesion failure reproducing faithfully through the new layer and a second rework cycle on the same article

anti_rework_rules.rule: Complete the log entry, with cause and lane outcome, before the case is closed
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-diagnosing the same defect from scratch next quarter and losing the trend that would have shown the systemic cause

iteration_protocol.trigger: the discriminating test returns an ambiguous result
iteration_protocol.action: change one different variable and re-run on coupons, never on customer goods; after two ambiguous results route the case as an unconfirmed most-likely cause rather than dressing it as fact

iteration_protocol.trigger: the same defect class recurs inside the scheduled recurrence window
iteration_protocol.action: demote the earlier cause to unconfirmed, reopen at the evidence triad with both runs' evidence side by side, and treat the failed prevention change as data

iteration_protocol.trigger: a replated piece fails again with the same defect class
iteration_protocol.action: stop further rework on that article, escalate from a lane fix to a systemic case, quarantine the related production and re-examine the disposition including return

iteration_protocol.trigger: the supplier changes a stripping or plating product, or issues a revised technical data sheet
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the hazard class, compatibility, segregation and waste route before the next use, and re-check the feasibility assumptions that depended on the old product

iteration_protocol.trigger: the counted log shows one lane or one defect class dominating the quarter
iteration_protocol.action: assemble the ranked evidence pack for that lane and treat it as a standing systemic case rather than as a queue of individual complaints

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect appears whose appearance no existing class describes
iteration_protocol.action: add a class with photographs and its separating question, and revisit the trees that should have caught it

iteration_protocol.trigger: field returns arrive showing corrosion or wear-through weeks after delivery
iteration_protocol.action: re-open the porosity and staining reasoning on the retained parts of those runs, refer the deposit question to the verification lane, and review the stack rather than the individual piece

iteration_protocol.trigger: a customer disputes the diagnosis or what was promised about the result
iteration_protocol.action: assemble the case file — photographs, axis answers, coupon result, test record, disposition and disclosure wording — and escalate to instrumented or send-out evidence where a claim depends on a number

priority_rationale: Intake and the no-blame attribution rule come first because they decide whether evidence and an honest hypothesis exist at all; the defect class library and the three evidence axes turn that evidence into a bounded question; witness replay and the one-variable coupon test are the two methods that convert a question into a cause; the seven cause trees each consume those answers to reach a candidate root cause in prep, chemistry, process or the evidenced substrate boundary; routing hands the confirmed cause to a single owning lane, after which disposition, strip feasibility, documented approval, stripping safety and waste, and the reset replate govern what happens to the goods in strict order of irreversibility; and the log, the disclosure discipline and the prevention loop come last because they are what turns one closed case into a shop that stops making the defect.
